title: Connection budget: reduce to three evaluators
notes: LaunchDarkly meters average concurrent SDK connections with a ceiling of five. Thirty-two evaluators burned 3.761 of that in four days and would have hit the limit within a day. Measured cost is 0.975 concurrent per evaluator, against a predicted 0.005 — wrong by roughly two hundred times.

Short-lived clients reconnecting every five minutes are not cheaper than one held open. Either close() does not release the stream promptly, or reconnects are billed with a minimum duration. The earlier conclusion that short-lived connections were validated came from a single reading taken before the container count was raised, and measured the wrong configuration.

Three survivors chosen for coverage rather than convenience. demo-orders on Production and Staging carries demo-email-notifications-v2 plus all three false-silence controls in both critical environments. demo-checkout on Production carries demo-tax-calculation-v2 and five other flags. Both archive candidates and every control stay alive.

Volume is free; connections are what cost. One evaluator covering seven flags at high rate costs the same as one covering a single flag, which is why the cut is by container count and not by traffic rate.
Projected August close at three evaluators is 4.80 of 5. September starts fresh and the tier ladder in scenario/budget.json defines what to run at each level of remaining headroom.
